::: {.work-intro}
My experience moves from the lab to the field: doctoral and postdoctoral research at UC San Diego, then engineering practice in Germany. Along the way, teaching and mentoring became an important part of the work. The most recent role comes first.

## R&D Engineer

::: {.organization}
LPI Ingenieurgesellschaft mbH
:::

At LPI, I brought my research background to bridges in service, working on structural monitoring and condition assessment.

- Automated operational modal analysis of long-term monitoring data, with bootstrap uncertainty bounds.
- Studied how temperature shifts the natural frequencies of two twin bridges, one with documented tendon damage.
- Interpreted strain, displacement, inclination, acoustic-emission, and fiber-optic measurements for bridge owners, and automated parametric SOFiSTiK models with Python.

::: {.case-links}
[Operational Modal Analysis and Temperature Effects →](work/bridge-oma-temperature.qmd)

## Postdoctoral Researcher

::: {.organization}
University of California San Diego
:::

After my Ph.D., I extended the USACE/ERDC-supported research program from single structures to populations of similar structures, and tested the corrosion model against experiments.

- Developed generalized damage diagnosis that uses labeled data from one structure to diagnose a similar, unlabeled structure.
- Validated Bayesian updating of the corrosion model against laboratory corrosion experiments.
- Contributed to proposals and semiannual sponsor reviews, and mentored graduate and undergraduate researchers.

::: {.case-links}
[Generalized Damage Diagnosis →](work/generalized-damage-diagnosis.qmd) · [Bayesian Model Updating →](work/corrosion-model-updating.qmd)
:::

## Graduate Student Researcher

::: {.organization}
University of California San Diego
:::

My doctoral research asked how to diagnose and predict pitting corrosion in large civil infrastructure.

- Built a multiphysics phase-field corrosion model and machine-learning surrogates that run it in seconds.
- Propagated uncertainty from loads, chemistry, and models to a reliability analysis of an entire gate.
- Developed Bayesian model updating from inspection images.

::: {.case-links}
[Corrosion Simulation →](work/corrosion-simulation.qmd) · [Uncertainty and Reliability →](work/corrosion-reliability.qmd) · [Bayesian Model Updating →](work/corrosion-model-updating.qmd)
:::

## Teaching

Teaching assistant for SE 168/268, *Structural System Testing and Model Correlation* (Spring 2022 and 2023), a course co-taught by Prof. Michael Todd and engineers from ATA Engineering. Over ten weeks, students take a plate from a finite-element model to a modal test, signal processing, test–model correlation, and model updating.

I led lab instruction in instrumentation, hammer and shaker testing, data acquisition, and data quality, and guided students through modal identification and correlation. In the final project, students locate a hidden spring and estimate its stiffness from new measurements.

::: {.case-links}
[Structural Vibration Testing and Model Correlation →](work/vibration-testing-model-correlation.qmd)
:::

I also supported SE 130A/B, *Structural Analysis I and II* (Summer 2021).
:::
